items.title: Nestlé to sell ice cream unit to Froneri in major overhaul

featured_image.name: Nestlé Headquarter | Vevey, VD - Switzerland. Siège Social d ...

items.description:
Nestlé, the world's largest food and beverage company, announced Thursday that it will sell its remaining ice cream business to joint venture partner Froneri as part of a sweeping corporate overhaul aimed at streamlining operations around four core categories.

The Swiss giant, known for KitKat chocolate bars and Nescafé coffee, said it is in "advanced negotiations" to transfer the ice cream division, which includes brands like Häagen-Dazs, to Froneri—a joint venture Nestlé created in 2016 with private equity firm PAI Partners. Under the restructuring, the company will concentrate resources on coffee, petcare, nutrition, and food and snacks.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Samsung shares hit record high on report of higher AI chip prices

featured_image.name: Samsung raised memory chip prices by up to 60% since September, according to reports — AI data center build out strangles supply

items.description:
Samsung Electronics stock surged to an all-time high on Thursday after local media reported the South Korean tech giant is negotiating sharply higher prices for its next-generation AI memory chips, signaling a potential turnaround in its competitive battle with smaller rival SK Hynix.

The chipmaker's shares jumped as much as 5.4% to a record 190,900 won on the Korea Exchange, closing at 190,000 won as trading resumed following a three-day holiday. The rally comes amid renewed optimism for technology stocks globally, with the Nasdaq Composite rising 0.8% on Wednesday as investors returned to semiconductor and software sectors.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Study finds most people overconfident in spotting AI faces

featured_image.name: Research Finds Overconfidence in Spotting AI-Generated Faces ...

items.description:
New research from Australian universities reveals that people's confidence in their ability to identify artificial intelligence-generated faces far exceeds their actual detection skills, leaving individuals and organizations vulnerable to deception.

The study, published this week in the British Journal of Psychology by researchers at UNSW Sydney and the Australian National University, found that even "super-recognizers"—individuals with exceptional face-recognition abilities—struggled to distinguish AI-generated faces from real ones.[1][2]

items.title: Penn State researchers develop polymer capacitor for extreme heat

featured_image.name: New polymer alloy could solve energy storage challenge

items.description:
Researchers at Pennsylvania State University have developed a new polymer capacitor capable of storing four times the energy of conventional models while operating at temperatures up to 482 degrees Fahrenheit, addressing a long-standing limitation in electronics for electric vehicles, data centers, and space exploration systems.

The findings, published Tuesday in Nature, describe a "polymer alloy" made from two inexpensive, commercially available plastics that self-assemble into a stable nanostructure when combined.[1][2]

items.title: Oil jumps 4% as Vance says Iran rejected U.S. demands in talks

featured_image.name: Oil jumps 4% after Vance says Iran ignored key U.S. demands, military strikes on the table

items.description:
Oil prices recorded their largest single-day gain in four months on Wednesday after Vice President JD Vance said Iran refused to accept core U.S. demands in nuclear talks, and the Trump administration signaled military action remains on the table if diplomacy fails.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled up $2.86, or 4.59%, at $65.19 per barrel, while Brent crude gained $2.93, or 4.35%, to close at $70.35 per barrel, both benchmarks posting their highest settlements since late January. The rally marked the biggest one-day percentage increase for WTI since October 23.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: China fossils redated as oldest Homo erectus in East Asia

featured_image.name: Ancient skull uncovered in China could be million-year-old ...

items.description:
Crushed skulls unearthed in central China decades ago are now confirmed to be the oldest Homo erectus remains ever found in situ in eastern Asia, according to new research published this week in Science Advances. The finding rewrites the timeline of early human migration from Africa to the far reaches of the continent.

Using a sophisticated dating technique applied to quartz sediments at the Yunxian site in Hubei Province, an international team of researchers determined the fossils are approximately 1.77 million years old — roughly 600,000 to 800,000 years older than previous estimates suggested.[1][2][3]

items.title: Meta deal and India partnerships drive Nvidia-led market rally

featured_image.name: Nvidia in focus: Meta partnership expanded, Arm stake sold

items.description:
Nvidia propelled U.S. and Indian stock markets higher on Wednesday, as fresh partnerships in artificial intelligence infrastructure lifted major indexes and ignited rallies across technology and semiconductor stocks.

The S&P 500 rose 0.6% while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%, marking the third consecutive session of gains for both indexes. Nvidia's stock climbed as investor optimism mounted following a multiyear partnership announcement with Meta Platforms, which will deploy millions of the chipmaker's current and next-generation GPUs and CPUs in its AI data centers.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: Indonesia to deploy 8000 troops for Gaza peace mission by June

featured_image.name: Prabowo arrives in Washington for bilateral, Board of Peace ...

items.description:
Indonesia has announced that up to 8,000 soldiers will be prepared for deployment to Gaza by the end of June as part of the UN-authorized International Stabilization Force, marking the first firm commitment of military personnel to the multinational peacekeeping effort in the war-torn enclave.

Indonesian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Donny Pramono told the Associated Press on Sunday that the military has finalized its proposed troop structure and timeline, with an advance team of approximately 1,000 personnel expected to be ready for deployment as early as April. The decision comes as Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto arrived in Washington on Tuesday ahead of the inaugural Board of Peace summit scheduled for February 19.[1][2][3]

items.title: Study shows fire-prone weather days nearly tripled globally in 45 years

featured_image.name: Climate change has doubled western US forest fires, says ...

items.description:
The number of days when hot, dry, and windy weather creates ideal conditions for extreme wildfires has nearly tripled worldwide over the past 45 years, with researchers concluding that human-caused climate change drives more than half of this increase.

A study published Wednesday in Science Advances found that from 1979 through 1993, the world averaged about 22 "synchronous fire weather" days annually—periods when multiple regions simultaneously face conditions ripe for dangerous blazes. By 2023 and 2024, that figure had surged to more than 60 days per year.[1][2][3][4]
